messages:
maria (prod): Quick triage — we need to decide packaging for the Dedicated/Reserved offering by EOW. Customer asks are pushing for predictable commit + burst capability. Do we do one SKU with addons or separate SKUs?
aj (sales): Most enterprise buyers want a single line item they can commit to. Burst as a metered add-on is easiest to sell to Procurement.
lee (finance): Prefer separate metered add-on for clear revenue recognition. Also need minimum commitment thresholds to avoid churn risk.
nate (eng): Implementation notes: burst as a token-credit pool per-customer is doable. Rough ETA: 6w backend + 2w rollout/QA. Need design for KV cache isolation per-pool.
sophia (cs): Important launch criteria from customers: migration guide, per-project hard limits, clear overage policy, and a self-serve toggle in Console for burst on/off.
maria (prod): Draft launch checklist:
```
- Pricing SKU definition + contract language
- Commit cadence (monthly/annual) + min commitment
- Burst mechanics (pool size, refill, expiry)
- Console UX for toggles + usage surface
- Docs + migration guide + sales playbook
- SLOs and fallback policy defined
```
aj (sales): For contract constraints: customers ask for 99.9% uptime SLA on Dedicated and contractual guarantees on reserved throughput. They also want predictable upgrade/downgrade terms.
lee (finance): We should cap burst credits to avoid open-ended liabilities. Recommend "soft cap + admin approval" when usage exceeds 2x commit in a billing period.
nate (eng): Fallback option when Dedicated is saturated: auto-route to shared host model with degraded latency + notify customer. That policy needs to be explicit in contract.
maria (prod): Two packaging options on the table:
- Option A: One "Dedicated Premium" SKU (commit) + optional "Burst Pack" metered add-on
- Option B: Two SKUs: "Dedicated" (baseline) and "BurstPack" as standalone purchasable SKU
Vote quick: A/B?
aj (sales): A :thumbsup:
lee (finance): B — prefer separate product line for accounting :thinking_face:
nate (eng): leaning A but neutral — A makes UX simpler, B simpler for finance
sophia (cs): A — easier to explain to customers and to include in migration docs
maria (prod): A from me. Consensus trending A. Next: define limits and contract wording.
legal-bot: Reminder: include explicit fallback clause, overage billing cadence, and a force-majeure capacity clause for cross-region failovers.
maria (prod): Action items:
- aj (sales): draft sales playbook + suggested commit thresholds by Wed
- lee (finance): propose min-commit math and soft-cap policy by Thu
- nate (eng): prototype burst-credit system + fallback tests (6w estimate)
- sophia (cs): outline migration + support runbook by Thu
- maria (prod): draft pricing page copy + contract bullets by Fri
Please add if I missed anything.
aj (sales): I'll include a few customer-case examples in the playbook to justify thresholds.
lee (finance): Also add an experiment plan: launch with 2 price points, measure conversion and overage incidence.
maria (prod): Good — we'll reconvene next Tue for final signoff. If anyone needs to escalate, ping me directly. :v:
